title: Mount Nemrut near Lake Van erupted at end of Pleistocene
place_text: Mount Nemrut, southwest of Lake Van, Turkey

tellings.quote: exploded and you learn that that mountain last exploded at during the end of the pine during the younger and older dras

plain: Mount Nemrut, a volcano southwest of Lake Van in eastern Turkey, last erupted at the very end of the last ice age, around the cold spells geologists call the Older and Younger Dryas. That is what the researcher Matt LaCroix tells Michels, summing it up without naming a source. He raises it in a conversation about a great upheaval around 12,000 BC, and if he is right, the eruption would be one more sign of turmoil at that moment.
